items.title: Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content
items.publisher: European Commission (AI Office); drafted by independent chairs
items.why: Source of the quotation. Voluntary. Two layers (digitally signed metadata plus imperceptible watermark) for audio, image, video and containerised text; watermark alone for free-form text; fingerprinting or logging optional and not sufficient alone. Published 10 June 2026; found adequate by the Commission on 8 July 2026. Linked from digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/code-practice-ai-generated-content.

items.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), Article 50: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
items.publisher: European Commission, AI Act Service Desk
items.locator: Article 50(2) and 50(4); see also Article 2(1)(a) and (c) on the same site
items.why: The marking duty on providers and the disclosure duty on deployers. This is the Commission's copy, not the Official Journal (EUR-Lex returned empty pages). The page carries a notice that the provision was amended by the Digital Omnibus and the displayed text is not yet updated; paragraphs 2 and 4 are not flagged as amended.

items.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), Article 111: AI systems already placed on the market
items.publisher: European Commission, AI Act Service Desk
items.locator: Article 111(4), marked NEW; with Article 113 (general application from 2 August 2026)
items.why: Source of the dates. Systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 must comply with the marking duty by 2 December 2026. Commission's copy; carries the same 'not yet updated' notice although the new paragraph is displayed.

items.title: Deepfake Defences 2: The Attribution Toolkit
items.locator: Key takeaways 5 and 8 (pp. 6-7); Box 2 (p. 14); survey findings (pp. 25-26)
items.why: Source of the figure. A discussion paper, not guidance: Ofcom says regulated services are not required to adopt the measures. Says watermarks, metadata and labels should be used in combination.

items.title: Report on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
items.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Intellectual Property Office
items.locator: Section E: Output transparency (Overview; Conclusions and proposals); summary under 'Labelling of AI and human-created content'
items.why: The UK position in the government's own words: no obligation to label AI-generated content; proposal to work with industry on good practice. Published 18 March 2026.

items.title: Disclosure of AI in Advertising: Striking the Balance Between Creativity and Responsibility
items.publisher: Advertising Standards Authority and Committee of Advertising Practice
items.why: No blanket UK requirement to disclose AI in adverts; existing rules apply however content is made; a disclosure does not cure a misleading claim. An advice article, not a Code rule.
